'''Josephine Hughes Chanler''' (7 April 1906 – 23 December 1992) was an American mathematician specializing in [[algebraic geometry]].<ref name="pioneer"/>

== Early life and education ==
She was born in [[St. Louis, Missouri]]. She was the only child of Louisa Castle and James Chanler. Her parents separated soon after her birth, and she grew up with her mother, who lived in [[Bowling Green, Kentucky]] and worked as a schoolteacher. As a girl she became ill with [[polio]], and had to undergo treatment for it at intervals later in her life. When she was a high school student, she and her mother moved to [[Jacksonville, Florida]], but they moved back to Bowling Green so that Chanler could attend the [[Western Kentucky University|Western Kentucky State Normal School and Teacher's College]]. She completed a degree there in 1927, and became a high school teacher.<ref name="pioneer">{{cite book| first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940s PhDs|date=2009|publisher=American Mathematical Society|isbn=9780821843765|page=156|edition=Illustrated addition|title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics}} Biography on p.125-127 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

In 1929, Chanler and her mother moved again, to [[Illinois]], so that Chanler could begin graduate studies at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].
She earned a master's degree under the mentorship of [[Bessie Irving Miller]], but Miller died soon afterward.<ref name="pioneer"/>
She completed her doctorate there in 1933.<ref name="mathtimesspring1993">{{cite web|title=Math Times - Spring 1993|url=http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/MathTimesSP93.pdf|website=University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|accessdate=1 February 2017}}</ref><ref name="mathtimesfall1993">{{cite web|title=Math Times - Fall 1993|url=http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/MathTimesFA93.pdf|website=University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|accessdate=1 February 2017}}</ref> Her dissertation, ''Poristic Double Binary Forms'', was [[doctoral advisor|supervised]] by [[Arthur Byron Coble]].<ref name="genealogy">{{mathgenealogy|id=4150}}</ref>

== Career ==
After completing her PhD, she joined the faculty at Illinois,<ref name=S93>[https://math.illinois.edu/system/files/inline-files/MathTimesSP93.pdf University of Illinois website, ''Math Times'' magazine, Spring 1993, page 7]</ref> and became an associate professor in 1944.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1944-50-01/S0002-9904-1944-08056-7/S0002-9904-1944-08056-7.pdf   American Mathematical Society website, ''1944 bulletin: notes'', page 47]</ref> Despite an offer to move to a college in [[New England]], Chanler remained at Illinois for the rest of her career.<ref name="pioneer" /> She retired as an associate professor in 1971.<ref name="pioneer" />  After her retirement, she continued to tutor students.<ref name=S93 />
 
== Personal life ==
Chanler lived with her mother until her mother's death in 1948.<ref name="pioneer" />

Chanler was a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]], a member of [[Toastmasters International]], and a member of St. Mary's Catholic Church{{Which|date=July 2021}}.<ref name="pioneer" /> She listed her religion in about 1940 as [[Presbyterianism|Presbyterian]], but she described herself in a 1983 conversation as "a Southern Presbyterian–Calvinist–Catholic with leanings toward Judaism and Islam and a very high regard for Buddhism, Mormons, and some Hindu gods".<ref name="pioneer" />

Chanler died in [[Urbana, Illinois]] in 1992, having been in a health care facility{{Which|date=July 2021}} for five years prior; she is buried there at Mount Hope Cemetery.<ref name="pioneer" /> She was remembered as "an excellent teacher and a person that everyone seemed to admire" by Annette Sinclair, who once took a summer course in classical algebraic geometry with Chanler.<ref>{{Cite web|date= Fall 1993|title=Math Times|url=https://math.illinois.edu/system/files/inline-files/MathTimesFA93.pdf|access-date=5 July 2021|website=math.illinois.edu}}</ref>

== Legacy ==

The Josephine Chanler Scholarship for undergraduate students at UI was created in 2020 by Padmini Joshi.<ref>[https://math.illinois.edu/josephine-chanler-scholarship University of Illinois website, ''Josephine Chanler Scholarship'']</ref>
